requirements.requirement: Inventory application is served over TCP port 8181 on node1
requirements.summary: httpd was installed, configured with a VirtualHost on port 8181 serving /var/www/inventory. curl to $NODE_IP:8181 returned HTTP 200 with the expected inventory content both before and after a full node restart, and the after-executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms a listening socket on [::]:8181 owned by httpd processes.

requirements.requirement: SELinux (mandatory access control) remains in Enforcing mode throughout
requirements.summary: getenforce reports Enforcing at every checkpoint: before configuring httpd, while diagnosing the bind failure, after applying the semanage port fix, immediately before the restart, and after the restart. /etc/selinux/config also remained set to enforcing. No evidence of a permissive/disabled window at any point.

requirements.requirement: Access enabled via a genuine SELinux policy change rather than disabling/weakening MAC (falsify-before-commit)
requirements.summary: httpd was first started with the port unlabeled for HTTP use, producing a real bind failure (Permission denied) and a corresponding AVC name_bind denial against intermapper_port_t while still Enforcing. The fix was a targeted semanage port relabel (tcp/8181 -> http_port_t), after which httpd bound successfully and no further AVC denials for port 8181 occurred, including post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, post-restart recovery)
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id, Enforcing, httpd active/enabled, HTTP 200, port policy) was captured, a native reboot was issued via a backgrounded sudo command with the acknowledgement returning before disconnect, the node was polled until exec access returned with a fresh uptime, and post-restart evidence shows a differing boot_id, Enforcing mode, httpd active, HTTP 200 with correct content, the port policy persisted, and no new AVC denials. This is independently corroborated by the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot showing a new boot_id and the after-executor listening-sockets snapshot showing httpd bound on 8181.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — serving the inventory application on TCP 8181 on node1 while SELinux remains Enforcing — are directly and coherently satisfied, with a genuine SELinux port-relabel fix proven via a falsify-before-commit AVC denial rather than a MAC weakening. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with a proper pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, differing boot identity, and full post-restart recovery, corroborated by fixed lifecycle snapshots. The main blemish is an unauthenticated (gpgcheck=0) vault repo left permanently enabled to work around the offline package-repo environment, which was not cleaned up afterward.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency check (package-health) was unavailable (timed out) in both the before-prepare and after-executor lifecycle snapshots, so overall package integrity beyond the httpd/policycoreutils-python install cannot be independently confirmed.

No command in the trace shows the vault.repo file being removed or disabled after use, so its final enabled/disabled state can only be inferred as still present from the absence of any removal command.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were necessary and appropriately bounded: package installation for httpd/policycoreutils-python, the inventory content/vhost, and the semanage port relabel are all directly tied to the task. The offline node had no enabled subscription-manager repos, so enabling a temporary CentOS 7 vault repo (cmd-40c7ed3106c34c2a) to install httpd was a reasonable prerequisite. However, this vault.repo file uses gpgcheck=0 and was left enabled in /etc/yum.repos.d/ with no observed cleanup/disable step afterward, despite the executor's own summary describing it as 'temporary' — this is a retained, unauthenticated third-party repo that weakens future package-install integrity on the node and was not reverted. A brief failed diagnostic attempt to add the port mapping with `semanage port -a` (cmd-17debe1de5874062) errored out (port already defined) and caused no state change, so it is not penalized. The initial httpd start that failed to bind (cmd-b18921fc50784845) was a deliberate falsify-before-commit step directly supporting the SELinux-genuineness outcome, not an unnecessary mutation. No abandoned files, conflicting services, or damaged package state were otherwise observed; /tmp/reboot.log is a benign, low-risk artifact of the reboot command.
